To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The interference among devices using the same spreading factor has a significant impact on the network performance; (2) The interference between different spreading factors also plays a crucial role in determining the network performance; and (3) The network performance can be improved by increasing the spreading factor of devices.
the performance of a single cell LoRa network is significantly affected by the imperfect orthognality of SFs, which is not considered in the current LoRaWAN specification.

the network scalability is significantly lower than what is currently assumed.
the network scalability is limited by the number of devices per SF.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the network performance is more sensitive to co-SF than inter-SF interference.
the network performance of LoRaWAN under co-SF and inter-SF interference is considerably pessimistic and should be considered in the network design.
, while a single SF can support a high density of devices, the inter-SF interference can significantly reduce the scalability performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a LoRa network is severely impacted by the inter-SF interference, which has been overlooked in previous studies.
the performance of LoRaWAN is more sensitive to the interference among transmissions using different SFs than the interference among transmissions over a single SF.

the network scalability performance is significantly impacted by the imperfect orthognality of the spreading factor, and that the inter-SF interference is a dominant factor that should be accounted for when evaluating the network performance.
